stem.text: People enter a park at a rate of E(t) people per hour, where E is differentiable and t is measured in hours after the park opens. Measured values are E(0) = 25, E(2) = 45, E(4) = 70, E(6) = 50. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{6} E(t)\,dt \), the number of people who enter the park from t = 0 to t = 6, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 2 \cdot \frac{25 + 45}{2} = 70 \); \( 2 \cdot \frac{45 + 70}{2} = 115 \); \( 2 \cdot \frac{70 + 50}{2} = 120 \).

distractor_derivations.B: trapezoid area taken as width times the sum of the two endpoint values, with no division by 2
distractor_derivations.C: factor 1/2 applied to the last trapezoid only
distractor_derivations.D: right Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
